title: `logging/setLevel`
description: A request setting the minimum severity the server should emit for the rest of the session.
question: Does this framework let a caller set the server log level?
why: Session-scoped log level is a stateful control. 2026-07-28 replaced it with a per-request `_meta` field.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: `MCPServerAdapter` has no log-level API. Its sessions are private (`_adapter.sessions`) and run on the adapter's own event loop thread.
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `setLoggingLevel` works and the server honoured it, but @genkit-ai/mcp has no API for it and registers no notification handler; it works only on the SDK `Client` that the public getter `GenkitMcpClient.mcpClient` hands out (route `session`).
notes.langchain: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the adapter has no log-level API of its own. `MultiServerMCPClient.session()` hands out the raw mcp `ClientSession`, and `set_logging_level` on that session works.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: `MCPClient` exposes no log-level API. It sets a level per request through `serverLogLevel` instead. The SDK client's `setLoggingLevel` sits behind the private `mcpClientsById` field.
notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: the adapter has no log-level API. `MCPServerStdio.session` is the raw mcp `ClientSession`, and `set_logging_level` on it works.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no log-level API. `MCPSessionManager.create_session()` hands out the raw mcp `ClientSession`, and `set_logging_level` on it works.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` has no `logging/setLevel` method, and its session is private to `McpSessionActor`.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` has no `logging/setLevel` method, and its `ClientSession` is private (`_background_thread_session`).
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient has no `logging/setLevel` method, and `createMCPClient` offers no public route to send one.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `MCPServer` has no `logging/setLevel` method. The MCP client that has `setLoggingLevel` sits in the node shim's `session` field, which the SDK types as protected.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` has no logging-level method, and its sessions exist only inside the private `_run_session`, so no caller can send `logging/setLevel`.
notes.pi: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` has no setLevel method. The public generic `request('logging/setLevel', { level })` reaches the server, which then filters its logs, but the caller names the wire method.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: reachable only on a raw `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Client` from `MCPSessionManager.createSession()`, a public export of `@google/adk/tools/mcp` (`setLoggingLevel`). `MCPToolset` has no logging API.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` has no `logging/setLevel` method; the request works only through `MCPTools.session`, the fastmcp `Client` it exposes (`Client.set_logging_level`).
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so there is no route to `logging/setLevel`.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `MCPClient` has no log-level API. The session lives on the private `MCPClient._adapter` and runs on the adapter's own event loop thread.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no logging API. `logging/setLevel` works only through `set_logging_level` on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: the starter's API has no level setter. `McpSyncClient.setLoggingLevel` on the client bean the starter publishes works (at `warning` the server sent 2 of its 5 messages), so this goes through the session rather than the adapter.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no logging API. `logging/setLevel` is sent only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks, via `ClientSession.set_logging_level`.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): there is no API that sends `logging/setLevel` or names a log level for an MCP server.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has no log-level API. `logging/setLevel` works only through the public `MCPClient.session` (`session.set_logging_level(...)`), a raw MCP `ClientSession`, which the probe used.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: No ADK API. `McpTool.getMcpSession().setLoggingLevel` on the underlying `McpSyncClient` works: at `warning` the server sent 2 of 5 messages.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpClient` has no `logging/setLevel` method, so `DefaultMcpClient` never sends one.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no Koog API. `Client.setLoggingLevel` on the underlying Kotlin SDK `Client` works: at `warning` the server sent 2 of 5 messages.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `SetLoggingLevel` on.
